Inputs Situation a) Water Reservoir Status: As of March 06, 2025, the live storage in 155 major reservoirs is 89.83 BCM (50% of total capacity). Storage is at 120% of last year’s level and 117% of the 10-year average. The overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period. b) Groundwater Levels: Approximately 66.6% of monitoring wells show water levels between 0-5 m, while 29.1% report levels between 5-10 m. Decadal analysis (2014–2023) indicates a rise in 64.9% of wells and a decline in 35.1% as of August 2024. c) Seeds and Fertilizers: For Rabi 2024-25, certified seed availability is 337.98 lakh quintals against a requirement of 307.07 lakh quintals, ensuring a surplus of 30.90 lakh quintals. The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products. 6. Pests & Diseases: Intensity of pests and diseases, at some fields, has been reported to be above Economic Threshold Level for Wheat (Yellow rust) in Punjab. The Advisory has been issued by the survey team to the farms and regular monitoring is being carried out. The overall intensity of pests and diseases remained below Economic Threshold Level. 7. chunks.heading: Details of each Segment
chunks.text:
During the week (27th Feb 2025 – 05th Mar 2025), better rainfall was observed, as compared to Long Period Average (LPA) by 522%. Cumulative seasonal rainfall (01 Jan to 28th Feb 2025) is lower than LPA by 47%. Rainfall Forecast: 06th Mar – 12th Mar 2025 a) A fresh Western Disturbance is likely to affect Western Himalayan region from 09th March, 2025. Under its influence; Scattered to fairly widespread light/moderate rainfall/snowfall likely over Jammu-Kashmir-Ladakh-Gilgit-Baltistan-Muzaffarabad & Himachal Pradesh during 09th – 12th and Isolated light/moderate rainfall/snowfall likely over Uttarakhand during 10th -12th March. b) No significant weather likely over rest parts of the country during the week. 13th Mar - 19th Mar, 2025 c) Under the influence of western disturbances, scattered to fairly widespread rainfall/snowfall is likely over Western Himalayan Region during first half of week2. d) Light/moderate scattered to fairly widespread rainfall is also likely over northeast India and south Peninsular India during some days of the week.

chunks.heading: 2. TEMPERATURE: MIN & MAX
chunks.text:
Temperature Forecast 06th Mar – 12th Mar 2025 a) Gradual rise in maximum temperatures by 3-5°C likely over Northwest, central India and Gujarat State during next 4-5 days. b) No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over East India during next 2 days and gradual rise by about 2-3°C thereafter. c) No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over Maharashtra during next 24 hours and gradual rise by 2-4°C thereafter. 13th Mar - 19th Mar, 2025 d) Maximum temperatures are likely to be above normal by 2-3°C over many parts of northwest India and along west & east coast of India. It is likely to be near normal or below normal over rest parts of the country. e) There is a low to moderate probability of heatwave conditions over interior Odisha and north Coastal Andhra Pradesh. f) Minimum temperatures are likely to be below normal or near normal over most parts of the country except parts of coastal Karnataka, where it will be 2-3°C above normal.
